{{nihongo|'''Fuse Shrine'''|布制神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in Fusegomei Shimo-roku-tan, Shinonoi, {{ill|Nagano (city)|Q128849|qid=Q128849}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. {{nihongo|'''Fuse Shrine'''|布制神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

In addition to this shrine (Shinonoi Fusegomei), there are two other shrines with the same name within the same area ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinonoi Ishikawa}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinonoi Yamabuse}}).

The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420}}, with associated deities {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime-Ōkami}}, {{ill|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata|Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Yasakatome|ja|八坂刀売神|simple|Yasakatome|zh|八坂刀賣神|qid=Q9150392|lt=Yasaka Tome-no-Mikoto}}. Within the precincts, in addition to the heiden (offering hall), there are a mikoshi hall, various small shrines, and the enshrined divine spirit of {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|ca|Kitano Tenmangū|de|Kitano Tenman-gū|el|Ιερό Κιτάνο Τενμάνγκου|es|Kitano Tenman-gū|fa|کیتانو تنمانگو|fi|Kitano Tenman-gū|fr|Kitano Tenman-gū|it|Santuario Kitano|ja|北野天満宮|jv|Kitano Tenmangū|ko|기타노 덴만구|la|Kitano Tenmangū|my|ခိတနိုတန်းမန်းဂူး|ru|Китано-Тэммангу|si|කිතනෝ තෙන්මන්ගූ|simple|Kitano Tenman-gū|sv|Kitano-tenmangū|tr|Kitano Tenman-gū|zh|北野天滿宮|qid=Q662176}}, among others.

== Overview ==
This shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420}}. The date of its founding is ancient; it is listed in the “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}” (927), the oldest extant record of official shrines in Japan, but the exact year of establishment is unknown.

The previous shrine buildings collapsed due to the {{ill|1847 Zenkoji earthquake|ar|زلزال زينكوجي 1847|es|Terremoto de Zenko-ji de 1847|fr|Séisme de 1847 à Nagano|ja|善光寺地震|ko|젠코지 지진|zh|善光寺地震|qid=Q11418893}}, and were rebuilt in {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} 4 (1851). Due to deterioration, a complete reconstruction was carried out in September of {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 15 (2003), resulting in the current buildings.

At the innermost part of the shrine complex is the main hall, built in {{ill|Culture|Q11042|qid=Q11042}} 6 (1809) in the nagare-zukuri style of a one-bay shrine, richly decorated with carvings themed on {{ill|kachōfūgetsu|Q11615743|qid=Q11615743}} (flowers, birds, wind, and moon).

・{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fuse Honshō}} is said to have been the name of this shrine’s estate.

・Toward the end of the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, local youths attempted to loot the {{ill|Senryū-Shōgunzuka Kofun|Q17222794|qid=Q17222794}}. Astonished by the quantity of buried items, they reported the matter to the {{ill|Matsushiro Domain|Q903575|qid=Q903575}}. Following the domain’s decision that the excavated items be deposited at this shrine, they were preserved as the shrine’s treasures. Some were later transferred to the {{ill|Nagano City Museum|Q11654184|qid=Q11654184}}.

== Shrine precincts ==
Within the precincts are the mikoshi hall, Ten’ō Shrine (Tsushima Shrine), Sericulture Shrine, Akiba Shrine, Konpira Shrine, Kōtaijingū, Yama-no-Kami Shrine, Tenman Shrine, Iizuna Shrine, Tarō Shrine, Jijū Shrine, and the shrine of Kitano Tenman-gū.

* Mikoshi Hall  
A palace-style mikoshi used during the Gion Festival is housed here. The festival began to commemorate Fuse Village’s elevation to town status as Shinonoi Town in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 3 ({{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}}).

The Gion Festival is held on the last Saturday and Sunday of July. On the Sunday one week prior, a ritual called “Ten’ō-oroshi” is performed, in which the sacred object of the Ten’ō Shrine (Tsushima Shrine) enshrined within the precincts is placed on a mikoshi and transferred to a temporary shrine set up along Shinonoi Station Street. On the final day, the “Ten’ō-age” rite is conducted, after which the mikoshi is returned to the Mikoshi Hall.

== Location ==
235 Shinonoi Fusegomei, Nagano City, Nagano Prefecture

== Access ==
About a 10-minute walk from {{ill|Shinonoi Station|Q5357193|qid=Q5357193}} on {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}} and {{ill|Shinano Railway|Q11254401|qid=Q11254401}} lines
